text: effective_cores() safe default size thread pool worker pool. takes smallest host's logical CPUs, process's CPU affinity, cgroup cpuset cgroup CPU quota (rounded , since 1.5-core quota can keep 2 threads busy). Inside container often much smaller parallel::detectCores().

text: object class fax: x$cpu x[["cpu"]] returns namespace nested list values. x[["cpu.host"]] returns group facts way. x[["cpu.effective"]] returns value single fact. names(x) lists available namespaces. .list(x) resolves returns default namespaces.

title: Current CPU and memory usage, cheap enough for every log line — usage
text: usage(): named numeric vector class fax_usage time: sample taken, seconds since epoch. cpu_process: CPU cores used R process since previous call. cpu_cgroup: CPU cores used whole container since previous call, including processes parallel workers. cpu_throttled: share CPU scheduling periods since previous call container throttled hitting CPU quota. cpu_limit: CPU cores process may use (see effective_cores()). mem_rss: resident memory process, bytes. mem_cgroup: memory used container, including page cache. mem_limit: memory limit (see effective_memory()). mem_pct: mem_cgroup / mem_limit, mem_rss share host memory container. usage_line(): string "cpu=1.8/4 thr=3% mem=2.1G/8G(26%) rss=1.2G".

title: Current CPU and memory usage, cheap enough for every log line — usage
text: CPU values rates, compare previous call: first call reports process's average since started, cpu_cgroup cpu_throttled NA second call. fork() (e.g. parallel::mclapply() workers) baseline starts . macOS Windows, mem_rss needs ps package, container fields always NA.

title: fax (development version)
text: Initial CRAN submission. effective_cores() effective_memory() return CPU cores memory process can actually use, taking cgroup v1/v2 limits, cpusets CPU affinity account. facts(), fact() facts_df() provide lazy, cached snapshot facts per-fact status source. Resolver errors never escape unless strict = TRUE. Facts describe OS (os.*), CPU, memory cgroups, process runs: bare metal VM (virtualization.*, including WSL), container (container.*), Kubernetes pod (k8s.*, including Downward API) cloud provider (cloud.provider). usage() usage_line() report current process container CPU memory use cheaply enough call every log line.
